abstract: This fictional scenario separates definitions, observations, interpretations, sources and learning paths without evaluating any student.

context.text: Observations depend on temperature, wind and measurement conditions.

definition.text: Evaporation is the change from liquid water to water vapor.

examples.text: Water in a shallow dish may decrease over time.
A wet surface can dry without boiling.

limits.text: A lower water level alone does not establish the mechanism.
This card proposes a study path; it does not certify competency.

objective.text: Distinguish an observation from an interpretation supported by sources.

prerequisites.text: Recognize a liquid and read a measurement in a table.

reflection.text: What alternative explanation should be checked before drawing a conclusion?

steps.text: Observe and record the dish’s initial water level.
Record another measurement in the same location.
Compare the readings and identify unknown conditions.

limits.text: No real measurement or photograph is supplied in this demonstration.
